'''Malika Jeffries-EL''' is an American chemist and Senior associate dean of the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences at [[Boston University]] studying [[organic semiconductor]]s.<ref name=gs>{{Google scholar id}}</ref> Specifically, her research focuses on developing organic semiconductors that take advantage of the processing power of polymers and the electronic properties of semiconductors to create innovative electronic devices.<ref>{{Cite news|title=US Fed News|date=February 6, 2013|work=Chemist Takes Polymer Study on the Road}}</ref>  She was elected as a Fellow of the [[American Chemical Society]] in 2018.<ref name=":3" />

== Early life and education ==
Jeffries-EL is from Brooklyn, New York and was the first in her immediate family to attend college.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.wellesley.edu/news/2016/september/node/97721|title=BU Chemistry Professor Malika Jeffries-EL '96 Encourages Wellesley Students to Persevere in the Lab and in Life|website=Wellesley College|language=en|access-date=2018-08-24}}</ref> She was inspired to become a scientist by [[Mae Jemison]], an American engineer, physicist, and astronaut who was the first black woman to travel to space.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/opinion/pineapple-does-not-belong-on-pizza/3009324.article|title=Pineapple does not belong on pizza!|work=Chemistry World|access-date=2018-08-24|language=en}}</ref> Jeffries-EL earned BA degrees in Chemistry and [[Africana studies|Africana Studies]] from [[Wellesley College]] in 1996.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://www.bu.edu/chemistry/jeffries-el-3/|title=Malika Jeffries-EL " Chemistry {{!}} Boston University|website=www.bu.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-08-24|archive-date=2018-08-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825041251/http://www.bu.edu/chemistry/jeffries-el-3/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 1999 she earned her master's degree in chemistry from George Washington University (GWU). In 2002, Jeffries-EL completed her PhD in [[synthetic chemistry|Synthetic Chemistry]] at GWU.  Richard Tarkka supervised her.<ref name=phd/><ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://oxide.jhu.edu/2/board/jeffries-el|title=Prof. Malika Jeffries-EL|date=January 27, 2020|website=Open Chemistry Collaborative in Diversity Equity (OXIDE).}}</ref>

== Research and career==
After completing her PhD, Jeffries-EL worked as a postdoctoral fellow at [[Carnegie Mellon University]] under the supervision of [[Richard D. McCullough]] from 2002 to 2005.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news|url=https://www.cmu.edu/mcs/news-events/2018/0816_ACS_Fellows.html|title=Four Chemistry Alumni Named American Chemical Society Fellows – Mellon College of Science – Carnegie Mellon University|last=University|first=Carnegie Mellon|date=2018|access-date=2018-08-24|language=en|archive-date=2023-04-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230415173244/https://www.cmu.edu/mcs/news-events/2018/0816_ACS_Fellows.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2015 Jeffries-EL was selected as the 8th Annual Goldstein Distinguished Lecturer by [[Cal Poly Pomona College of Engineering]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cpp.edu/~sci/chemistry-biochemistry/index.shtml|title=Chemistry and Biochemistry|website=www.cpp.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-08-24}}</ref> She was the keynote speaker at the 2016 Northeastern Section of the [[American Chemical Society]] meeting.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nesacs.org/curr_events_news.html|title=Welcome to NESACS – Current Events {{!}} News|website=www.nesacs.org|access-date=2018-08-24}}</ref>

In 2016 she joined [[Boston University]] as a tenured associate professor.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bu.edu/chemistry/tag/jeffries-el/|title=Jeffries-EL " Chemistry {{!}} Boston University|website=www.bu.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-08-24}}</ref>
